sentences.text: The owner of the offending vehicle as well as the claimant are in appeal in respect of an accident which occurred on 18.06.2016 which resulted in the death of Manjunath, who was riding pillion in the motorcycle.

The Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.10,88,400/-
and has proceeded to exonerate the liability of the insurer on the ground that the owner of the offending vehicle did not possess a driving licence.

3. As far as liability is concerned, since it was the case of the insurer that the driver of the offending vehicle did not have a driving licence to drive a vehicle, it is obvious that it was putting forth the plea that there was a breach of policy conditions in light of the judgment rendered in Yallavva's1 case and in such cases, the insurer has to pay the compensation and thereafter recover the same from the owner of the offending vehicle after it pays the compensation to the claimants.
Consequently, the insurer is reserved with liberty to proceed against the owner of the offending vehicle.

To that extent,
the finding regarding liability is modified.

sentences.text: . As far as compensation is concerned, the Tribunal has recorded a finding that the deceased was earning a sum of Rs.7,000/- per month notionally since there was no evidence as to the actual income of the deceased.

In such circumstances, since the accident is of the year 2016, it would be appropriate to adopt the notional income determined by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, which would be Rs.9,500/-.

Since the deceased was aged 18 years, future prospects of 40% requires to be added to the same, which makes his income to be Rs.13,300/- (Rs.9,500/- +
Rs.3,800/-).

Since the deceased was a bachelor, 50% requires to be deducted from the same, which makes his income to be Rs.6,650/-.
5.

Thus, the claimants would be entitled to Rs.14,36,400/- (Rs.6,650/- X 12 X '18') towards 'loss of dependency'.
6.

The claimants would also be entitled to Rs.48,400/-
each towards loss of love and affection, which would NC: 2024:KHC:50719 be Rs.1,45,200/-
(Rs.48,400/- X 3 members).
They are also entitled to a sum of Rs.36,300/- towards miscellaneous expenses.

7. Thus, the claimants would be entitled to a sum of Rs.16,17,900/- as against Rs.10,88,400/- as compensation along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
8. The statutory deposit made by the owner of the offending vehicle in M.F.A. No.7856/2018 shall be made over to the claimants and the balance shall be paid by the insurer.

The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the amount of compensation awarded within two months from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment and thereafter shall recover the same from the owner of the offending vehicle.
9.
The other aspects of the Award of the Tribunal remain undisturbed.
The appeal filed by claimants is, accordingly, allowed in part and the appeal filed by owner of the offending vehicle is disposed of.
